title: A walking program and a plantar ulcer
objective: Apply the APTA diabetic foot ulcer guideline: prescribe exercise that keeps cardiovascular and muscular fitness while minimizing weight bearing, adding an assistive device when it helps balance and unloading

brief.situation: 09:00 in an outpatient clinic. You are the wound management physical therapist. Mr. Banerjee, 61, with type 2 diabetes and peripheral neuropathy, was referred by his primary care provider for 'a walking program, 10,000 steps a day'.
handover: He says his feet 'don't feel much' and he noticed blood on his sock last week.

Clinic policy: inspect the feet of every patient with diabetes before exercise; an open ulcer gets a non-weight-bearing program, offloading and a same-day message to the provider for wound care and podiatry.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

parts.modelAnswer: He has an open plantar ulcer he can't feel. A walking program would grind it deeper.

scoring.modelReasoning: For a person with a diabetic foot ulcer, exercise should keep cardiovascular and muscular fitness while minimizing weight bearing, adding an assistive device when it helps balance and unloading. Inspect the feet before any program; Mr. Banerjee's insensate plantar ulcer needs non-weight-bearing exercise, offloading and wound care, not 10,000 steps.
